_note: Original stories and folk tales retold in Buddy's own words. Each paragraph is rendered as one audio clip. Kept short on purpose (about 30 seconds each).

stories.title: The Thirsty Crow
paragraphs: Once upon a time, on a very hot day, a crow was flying in the sky. He was so thirsty! He found a pot, but the water was right at the bottom, and his beak could not reach it.
The crow had an idea! He dropped in pebbles, one by one. Plop, plop, plop! Slowly, the water came up to the top.
The crow drank and drank, and he was happy. The end. When we think hard and keep trying, we can solve big problems!

stories.title: The Lion and the Little Mouse
paragraphs: Once upon a time, a big lion caught a tiny mouse. Please let me go, squeaked the mouse. One day I will help you! The lion laughed, but he let her go.
Soon after, the lion got stuck in a hunter's net. The little mouse came running and nibbled the ropes. Nibble, nibble, snip! The lion was free!
Now they were best friends. The end. Even small friends can do big things!

stories.title: The Tortoise and the Hare
paragraphs: Once upon a time, a fast hare laughed at a slow tortoise. So they had a race! Zoom! The hare ran far ahead.
I have lots of time, said the hare, and he fell asleep under a tree. The tortoise kept walking. Step, step, step.
When the hare woke up, the tortoise was already at the finish line! The end. Slow and steady, and never giving up, wins the race!

stories.title: The Monkey and the Crocodile
paragraphs: Once upon a time, a monkey shared sweet jamun fruits with his friend, the crocodile. One day the crocodile said, Ride on my back to my house. My wife wants to eat your heart!
The monkey stayed calm. Oh dear, he said, I left my heart in the jamun tree! Take me back and I will get it.
The silly crocodile swam back, and the monkey jumped up into the tree, safe. The end. Staying calm helps us think of a clever idea!

stories.title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
paragraphs: All summer, a little ant carried food to her home, while a grasshopper sang and played.
Then cold winter came, and there was no food outside. The hungry grasshopper knocked on the ant's door, and the kind ant shared her food.
The grasshopper learned to get ready for tomorrow. The end. It is good to play, and it is good to plan ahead too!

stories.title: The Clever Rabbit and the Lion
paragraphs: Once upon a time, a greedy lion scared all the animals in the forest. One day, a little rabbit said, Another lion lives here, and he says he is the king!
Show me! roared the lion. The rabbit took him to a deep well. The lion saw his own reflection in the water. He thought it was another lion, and jumped in. Splash!
All the animals cheered for the little rabbit. The end. Using our brain is better than being big and strong!

stories.title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
paragraphs: Once there was a shepherd boy who shouted, Wolf! Wolf! just for fun. The villagers came running, but there was no wolf.
Then one day, a real wolf came! Wolf! Wolf! shouted the boy. But this time nobody came, because they thought it was another trick.
The end. When we always tell the truth, people will believe us when we need help.

stories.title: Tiny Seed Grows Up
paragraphs: Deep in the soil, a tiny seed was sleeping. I am so small, said the seed. What can I do?
The rain gave it water, and the sun kept it warm. Pop! A little green shoot came up, and every day it grew a little taller.
One day, the tiny seed had become a big mango tree, full of sweet mangoes to share. The end. Little by little, every day, we grow too!

stories.title: The Little Star Who Lost Her Way
paragraphs: High up in the night sky lived a little star named Tara. One night, she played too far away and got lost.
Tara asked the moon for help. Follow the fireflies, said the moon. The fireflies blinked their tiny lights, and led her all the way home.
Her family was waiting, and Tara twinkled brighter than ever. The end. When we feel lost or scared, it is good to ask for help.

stories.title: Chintu the Baby Elephant
paragraphs: Chintu was a baby elephant who wanted to help everyone, but he was still very small.
One day, a kitten got stuck high up in a tree. Chintu thought, I am small, but my trunk is long! He stretched it up, up, up, and the kitten climbed down safely.
Everyone cheered. Hooray for Chintu! The end. Everyone is good at something. What are you good at?

stories.title: The River That Shared
paragraphs: A happy river gave water to the deer, to the fields, and to the children who played beside it.
One hot summer, the river became very thin. So the people stopped throwing rubbish in it, and planted trees all around.
When the rains came, the river was big and happy again. The end. When we take care of nature, nature takes care of us.
